meta.notes: Meta interviews emphasize optimal solutions and clean code under time pressure. Expect multiple rounds of medium/hard problems with follow-up questions about trade-offs and alternative approaches.

google.notes: Google values correctness and scalability above all — interviewers push for O(n log n) or better solutions. Strong emphasis on explaining your reasoning clearly as you code and discussing space/time trade-offs.

amazon.notes: Amazon interviews blend coding with leadership principle discussions. Problems often have practical system-design flavors — expect questions around data structures for large-scale lookups and real-world constraints.

microsoft.notes: Microsoft focuses on well-structured, readable code and thorough testing. Interviewers value candidates who think out loud, handle edge cases explicitly, and can iterate from a brute-force to an optimized solution.

apple.notes: Apple interviews emphasize clean, production-quality code with an eye for performance. Expect deep dives into your solutions — be ready to analyze complexity, discuss edge cases, and refactor on the fly.

netflix.notes: Netflix targets senior engineers with high autonomy — interviews lean toward complex, open-ended problems and system design. Expect questions that test depth of knowledge in algorithms applied to streaming and large-scale data.

uber.notes: Uber interviews frequently involve geo-spatial and routing problems reflecting their core business. Strong emphasis on graph algorithms, optimization under constraints, and real-world problem framing.

bloomberg.notes: Bloomberg interviews reflect their finance domain — expect string/data-parsing heavy problems and real-world system design around market data. Communication and structured problem decomposition are valued highly.
